title: Wikipedia and Digital Currencies: Interplay Between Collective Attention and Market Performance

extraction.methodology_summary: The authors construct a trading signal based on the daily change in Wikipedia page views for cryptocurrency pages. Specifically, they examine the difference in page views between day t and t-1; if page views increase, they take a short position in the asset, and if page views decrease, they take a long position. The strategy is tested on 17 cryptocurrencies that support margin trading over the period from July 2015 to January 2019, and performance is compared against a price-momentum baseline strategy and a random trading strategy.
extraction.universe: 38 cryptocurrencies with a Wikipedia page, with the investment strategy tested on 17 marginally traded cryptocurrencies

key_findings: A simple trading strategy based on daily Wikipedia page views outperforms both random and price-based baseline strategies in terms of cumulative returns for most of the covered period prior to 2018.
Wikipedia page views and edit history are positively and robustly correlated with cryptocurrency market properties such as price, trading volume, and market share.
A small, tightly connected community of specialized editors is responsible for the majority of information production regarding cryptocurrencies on Wikipedia.
The outperformance of the Wikipedia-based investment strategy breaks down after January 2018 following major losses and structural shifts in the cryptocurrency market.
limitations: The trading strategy neglects transaction fees, which could significantly decrease actual profits in real scenarios.
The strategy ceases to be successful after January 2018 when the cryptocurrency market suffered major losses.
